doc.title: Ralph Sutton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995

title: Rock and roll and good versus bad music
summary: Rock and roll had no effect on him; there are only good and bad kinds of music.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Now you have seen a lot of styles in music come and go. Some of them have come and stayed. Can you tell us what some of the changes were in music that you really enjoyed, or some that you did not enjoy? Was there anything that happened since the ‘40s that has really been you think significant for you, as far as changes in music? Either positively or negatively?
Well I’m thinking of, how did the rock & roll revolution if you want to call it that, effect your employment? Did it have any effect on what you did?
Well you don’t make the same kind of money that rock & rollers made. But I’ve never paid any attention to it, because I never listened to it, and it doesn’t interest me. Simple as that.
There’s only two kinds of music you know?
Good and bad. I always try to stick on the one side.
Stick on the one side and play with the good guys too.
